The Helmet of Salvation
HEL-met
noun phrase
From the Greek perikephalaia, “that which is about the head,” the helmet, the fifth piece of the armour, figuring the hope of salvation that guards the believer’s mind.

📖 Biblical Definition

The helmet of salvation is the fifth piece of the whole armour of God: And take the helmet of salvation (Eph 6:17). As the helmet guarded the soldier’s head, the seat of life and thought, so the assurance and hope of salvation guard the believer’s mind against the despairing and doubting thoughts the adversary would lodge there. The apostle opens the figure more fully in another place, where he bids the saints take for an helmet, the hope of salvation (1Th 5:8); for it is the sure hope of final deliverance, the confident expectation of glory laid up in Christ, that keeps the head erect and the mind steadfast in the fight. The dictionary marks this helmet as the believer’s assurance: not a hope that may fail, but a lively hope grounded on the finished work of Christ and the faithfulness of God, which is sure and stedfast (Heb 6:19). When the wicked one would beat down the soul with doubts of pardon or fears of falling, the helmet of salvation lifts the head, for the saint knows in whom he hath believed (2Ti 1:12). So the Scripture teaches that the mind kept by the hope of salvation is kept from the discouragement that disarms a soldier; the believer who wears this helmet looks beyond the battle to the certain victory God has promised, and being assured of the end, he fights the harder and faints not, for his salvation is of the Lord and cannot fail.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The fifth piece of the armour, the hope of salvation that guards the believer’s mind against doubt and discouragement.

THE HELMET OF SALVATION, the fifth piece of the armour, guarding the believer’s mind.

As the helmet guarded the soldier’s head, so it guards the seat of thought.

Paul names it elsewhere the hope of salvation, the confident expectation of glory.

It keeps the mind from the doubts and despair the adversary would lodge there.

Assured of the end, the believer fights the harder and faints not.

📖 Key Scripture

Eph 6:17 — "And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God:"

1Th 5:8 — "But let us, who are of the day, be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love; and for an helmet, the hope of salvation."

Heb 6:19 — "Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast, and which entereth into that within the veil;"

2Ti 1:12 — "For the which cause I also suffer these things: nevertheless I am not ashamed: for I know whom I have believed, and am persuaded that he is able to keep that which I have committed unto him against that day."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A figure of Scripture; the helmet of salvation teaches that the hope of salvation guards the believer’s mind in the battle.

expand to see more

The helmet of salvation has drawn little redefinition, surviving as the fifth piece of the armour the apostle names. The dictionary records it that the reader may mark the hope of salvation that guards the mind against doubt and discouragement.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the believer’s mind is guarded by the hope of salvation. As the helmet covered the soldier’s head, so the assurance of final deliverance keeps the saint’s mind steadfast when the wicked one would beat it down with doubts of pardon or fears of falling. This hope is no uncertain wish but a lively hope, sure and stedfast as an anchor of the soul, grounded on the finished work of Christ and the faithfulness of God. The believer who wears this helmet knows in whom he hath believed, looks beyond the battle to the certain victory, and being assured of the end, fights the harder and faints not.
